table_result.name: //bigquery.googleapis.com/projects/royston-dev-8253/datasets/cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy/tables/customer_segment_history
table_result.overview: This table tracks the historical segmentation of customers. It records the different segments a customer belonged to over time. This data supports analysis of customer segment changes and their impact. It also enables understanding customer lifecycle within various segments.

fields.name: customer_id
fields.description: This column contains a unique identifier for each customer.

fields.name: segment
fields.description: This column contains the assigned segment for a customer.

fields.name: valid_from
fields.description: This column contains the date from which a customer's segment became active.

fields.name: valid_to
fields.description: This column contains the date until which a customer's segment was active.

queries.sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  COUNT(segment) AS segment_change_count,
  MIN(valid_from) AS first_segment_change,
  MAX(valid_to) AS last_segment_change
FROM
  `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customer_segment_history`
GROUP BY
  customer_id
HAVING
  COUNT(segment) > (
    SELECT
      APPROX_QUANTILES(segment_changes_per_customer, 100)[OFFSET(95)]
    FROM (
      SELECT
        customer_id,
        COUNT(segment) AS segment_changes_per_customer
      FROM
        `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customer_segment_history`
      GROUP BY
        customer_id
    )
  )
  AND DATE_DIFF(MAX(valid_to), MIN(valid_from), DAY) < 30
ORDER BY
  segment_change_count DESC;
queries.description: Identify customers who have an unusually high number of segment changes within a short period (e.g., 30 days), indicating potential data anomalies or highly volatile customer behavior.

queries.sql:
WITH CustomerSegmentDurations AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    segment,
    DATE_DIFF(valid_to, valid_from, DAY) AS segment_duration_days
  FROM
    `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customer_segment_history`
  WHERE
    valid_to IS NOT NULL AND valid_from IS NOT NULL
),
SegmentAverages AS (
  SELECT
    segment,
    AVG(segment_duration_days) AS avg_segment_duration_for_segment,
    STDDEV(segment_duration_days) AS stddev_segment_duration_for_segment
  FROM
    CustomerSegmentDurations
  GROUP BY
    segment
),
CustomerAvgDurations AS (
  SELECT
    csd.customer_id,
    csd.segment,
    AVG(csd.segment_duration_days) AS customer_avg_segment_duration,
    COUNT(csd.segment) AS segment_count,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY csd.customer_id ORDER BY COUNT(csd.segment) DESC) as rn
  FROM
    CustomerSegmentDurations csd
  GROUP BY
    csd.customer_id, csd.segment
)
SELECT
  cad.customer_id,
  cad.segment AS most_frequent_segment,
  cad.customer_avg_segment_duration,
  sa.avg_segment_duration_for_segment,
  sa.stddev_segment_duration_for_segment
FROM
  CustomerAvgDurations cad
JOIN
  SegmentAverages sa
ON
  cad.segment = sa.segment
WHERE
  cad.rn = 1
  AND cad.customer_avg_segment_duration < sa.avg_segment_duration_for_segment - (2 * sa.stddev_segment_duration_for_segment)
ORDER BY
  cad.customer_avg_segment_duration ASC;
queries.description: Find customers whose average segment duration is significantly shorter than the typical segment duration for their most frequent segment, suggesting unusual churn or rapid re-segmentation.

queries.sql: WITH SegmentEntryExit AS ( SELECT customer_id, segment, valid_from AS entry_date, LEAD(valid_from) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY valid_from) AS next_segment_entry_date, LEAD(segment) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY valid_from) AS next_segment FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customer_segment_history` ), ChurnEvents AS ( SELECT segment, COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS total_customers_in_segment, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN next_segment_entry_date IS NOT NULL AND DATE_DIFF(next_segment_entry_date, entry_date, DAY) <= 90 THEN customer_id ELSE NULL END) AS churned_customers FROM SegmentEntryExit GROUP BY segment ) SELECT segment, (churned_customers * 100.0 / total_customers_in_segment) AS churn_rate FROM ChurnEvents WHERE total_customers_in_segment > 0 ORDER BY churn_rate DESC LIMIT 5;
queries.description: Identify the top 5 segments with the highest churn rate, defined as the percentage of customers who moved out of a segment within 90 days of joining it.

queries.sql: WITH CurrentYearCustomers AS ( SELECT segment, COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS current_year_customer_count FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customer_segment_history` WHERE valid_from >= DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 1 YEAR) GROUP BY segment ), PreviousYearCustomers AS ( SELECT segment, COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS previous_year_customer_count FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customer_segment_history` WHERE valid_from >= DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 2 YEAR) AND valid_from < DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 1 YEAR) GROUP BY segment ) SELECT c.segment, (c.current_year_customer_count - COALESCE(p.previous_year_customer_count, 0)) * 100.0 / COALESCE(p.previous_year_customer_count, 1) AS percentage_growth FROM CurrentYearCustomers c LEFT JOIN PreviousYearCustomers p ON c.segment = p.segment ORDER BY percentage_growth DESC LIMIT 5;
queries.description: Find the segments that have experienced the most significant growth in customer count over the last year, measured by the percentage increase in unique customers.

queries.sql:
SELECT
  segment,
  VAR_SAMP(DATE_DIFF(valid_to, valid_from, DAY)) AS variance_in_segment_duration
FROM
  `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customer_segment_history`
GROUP BY
  segment
ORDER BY
  variance_in_segment_duration DESC
LIMIT 5;
queries.description: Identify customer segments that exhibit the highest variability in their membership duration, indicating potentially volatile or frequently changing customer statuses.

queries.sql:
SELECT
  AVG(segment_change_count) AS average_segment_changes,
  STDDEV_SAMP(segment_change_count) AS stddev_segment_changes
FROM (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    COUNT(DISTINCT segment) - 1 AS segment_change_count
  FROM
    `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customer_segment_history`
  WHERE
    valid_from BETWEEN '2023-01-01' AND '2023-12-31'
  GROUP BY
    customer_id
) AS customer_segment_changes;
queries.description: Calculate the average number of segment changes a customer undergoes within a specific time frame, and the standard deviation of these changes, to assess customer churn or migration patterns between segments.

queries.sql: WITH CustomerSegmentChanges AS ( SELECT customer_id, COUNT(segment) - 1 AS num_changes FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customer_segment_history` WHERE valid_from >= DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 2 YEAR) GROUP BY customer_id HAVING MAX(valid_to) >= DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 1 YEAR) ) SELECT APPROX_QUANTILES(num_changes, 2)[OFFSET(1)] AS median_segment_changes FROM CustomerSegmentChanges;
queries.description: Calculate the median number of segment changes for customers who have been active for at least one year, considering only their history within the last two years.

queries.sql:
SELECT
  segment,
  AVG(DATE_DIFF(valid_to, valid_from, DAY)) AS average_segment_duration_days,
  STDDEV_SAMP(DATE_DIFF(valid_to, valid_from, DAY)) AS stddev_segment_duration_days
FROM
  `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customer_segment_history`
GROUP BY
  segment
ORDER BY
  average_segment_duration_days DESC;
queries.description: Calculate the average duration a customer spends in each segment, along with the standard deviation of that duration, to understand segment stability and typical engagement periods.

queries.sql: SELECT segment, AVG(DATE_DIFF(valid_to, valid_from, DAY)) AS average_segment_duration_days FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customer_segment_history` WHERE DATE_DIFF(valid_to, valid_from, DAY) >= 30 GROUP BY segment ORDER BY average_segment_duration_days DESC LIMIT 5;
queries.description: Identify the top 5 customer segments with the highest average duration of segment membership, considering only segments that have been active for at least 30 days.

queries.sql: WITH CustomerActivity AS ( SELECT customer_id, COUNT(DISTINCT segment) AS distinct_segments, SUM(DATE_DIFF(valid_to, valid_from, DAY)) AS total_active_days FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customer_segment_history` GROUP BY customer_id HAVING SUM(DATE_DIFF(valid_to, valid_from, DAY)) >= 180 ) SELECT AVG(distinct_segments) AS average_segments_per_customer FROM CustomerActivity;
queries.description: Calculate the average number of segments a customer has been part of, considering only customers who have been active for at least 6 months in total.

queries.sql:
WITH SegmentConsecutiveDays AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    segment,
    valid_from,
    valid_to,
    DATE_DIFF(valid_to, valid_from, DAY) AS duration_days,
    LAG(valid_to) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id, segment ORDER BY valid_from) AS prev_valid_to
  FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customer_segment_history`
),
SegmentGroups AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    segment,
    valid_from,
    valid_to,
    duration_days,
    SUM(CASE WHEN valid_from = DATE_ADD(prev_valid_to, INTERVAL 1 DAY) THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id, segment ORDER BY valid_from) AS segment_group
  FROM SegmentConsecutiveDays
)
SELECT
  customer_id,
  segment,
  MIN(valid_from) AS continuous_period_start,
  MAX(valid_to) AS continuous_period_end,
  DATE_DIFF(MAX(valid_to), MIN(valid_from), DAY) AS total_continuous_days
FROM SegmentGroups
GROUP BY customer_id, segment, segment_group
HAVING DATE_DIFF(MAX(valid_to), MIN(valid_from), DAY) >= 365 -- Example: longer than 365 days
ORDER BY customer_id, segment, continuous_period_start;
queries.description: Identify customers who have been in a specific segment for a continuous period longer than a given threshold, using a rolling sum.

queries.sql:
WITH SegmentTransitions AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    segment,
    valid_from,
    LEAD(valid_from) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY valid_from) AS next_segment_start,
    valid_to
  FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customer_segment_history`
)
SELECT
  customer_id,
  segment,
  AVG(DATE_DIFF(COALESCE(next_segment_start, valid_to), valid_from, DAY)) AS avg_days_in_segment
FROM SegmentTransitions
GROUP BY customer_id, segment
ORDER BY customer_id, segment;
queries.description: Calculate the average time a customer stays in a specific segment before transitioning to another, or exiting.

queries.sql:
WITH CustomerSegmentCounts AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    segment,
    COUNT(*) AS segment_occurrence_count,
    SUM(DATE_DIFF(valid_to, valid_from, DAY)) AS total_days_in_segment,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, SUM(DATE_DIFF(valid_to, valid_from, DAY)) DESC) AS rn
  FROM
    `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customer_segment_history`
  GROUP BY
    customer_id, segment
)
SELECT
  customer_id,
  segment AS most_frequent_segment,
  total_days_in_segment
FROM
  CustomerSegmentCounts
WHERE
  rn = 1;
queries.description: For each customer, find the most frequent segment they belonged to and the total number of days they spent in that segment.

queries.sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  segment,
  valid_from,
  valid_to,
  DATE_DIFF(valid_to, valid_from, DAY) AS duration_in_segment_days
FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customer_segment_history`
ORDER BY customer_id, valid_from;
queries.description: Identify the duration each customer spent in a particular segment, considering segment changes over time.

queries.sql: WITH SegmentTransitions AS ( SELECT t1.customer_id, t1.segment AS from_segment, t2.segment AS to_segment, t1.valid_to AS transition_date FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customer_segment_history` t1 JOIN `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customer_segment_history` t2 ON t1.customer_id = t2.customer_id AND t2.valid_from > t1.valid_to AND DATE_DIFF(t2.valid_from, t1.valid_to, DAY) <= 90 ) SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) * 100.0 / (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customer_segment_history`) AS percentage_customers_transitioned FROM SegmentTransitions WHERE from_segment = 'Premium' AND to_segment = 'VIP';
queries.description: Determine the percentage of customers who have transitioned from one specific segment to another specific segment within a 90-day period.

queries.sql: SELECT customer_id FROM ( SELECT customer_id, COUNT(DISTINCT segment) AS distinct_segments, MAX(CASE WHEN valid_to = (SELECT MAX(valid_to) FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customer_segment_history` WHERE customer_id = t.customer_id) THEN DATE_DIFF(valid_to, valid_from, DAY) ELSE 0 END) AS days_in_current_segment FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customer_segment_history` t GROUP BY customer_id ) WHERE distinct_segments >= 3 AND days_in_current_segment > 180;
queries.description: Find the customer IDs who have been in at least 3 different segments and have spent more than 180 days in their current segment.

queries.sql: WITH InitialSegmentDurations AS ( SELECT customer_id, DATE_DIFF(MIN(valid_to) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY valid_from), MIN(valid_from) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY valid_from), DAY) AS initial_segment_duration FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customer_segment_history` QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY valid_from) = 1 ) SELECT AVG(initial_segment_duration) AS average_initial_segment_duration FROM InitialSegmentDurations;
queries.description: Determine the average number of days a customer spends in their initial segment before transitioning to another segment.

queries.sql:
WITH CustomerSegmentDurations AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    valid_from,
    valid_to,
    DATE_DIFF(valid_to, valid_from, DAY) AS duration_days,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY valid_from) AS rn
  FROM
    `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customer_segment_history`
)
SELECT
  CORR(t1.duration_days, t2.duration_days) AS correlation_initial_vs_subsequent_duration
FROM
  CustomerSegmentDurations t1
JOIN
  CustomerSegmentDurations t2
ON
  t1.customer_id = t2.customer_id
WHERE
  t1.rn = 1 AND t2.rn = 2;
queries.description: Determine the correlation between the length of a customer's initial segment membership and the length of their subsequent segment membership, to understand if early engagement duration predicts later engagement.

queries.sql:
WITH SegmentDurations AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    segment,
    DATE_DIFF(valid_to, valid_from, DAY) AS duration_days
  FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customer_segment_history`
),
TotalSegmentDuration AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    segment,
    SUM(duration_days) AS total_days_in_segment
  FROM SegmentDurations
  GROUP BY customer_id, segment
)
SELECT
  customer_id,
  segment,
  total_days_in_segment
FROM (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    segment,
    total_days_in_segment,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY total_days_in_segment DESC, segment ASC) AS rn
  FROM TotalSegmentDuration
)
WHERE rn = 1
ORDER BY customer_id;
queries.description: Determine the most frequent segment a customer has been in, based on the total time spent in each segment.
